expectations.text: Recognises that fabricated outputs have already been replaced with intent tables
expectations.evidence: D1 section states: 'Two intent tables are properly implemented' with details on both tables (lines 205-215 and 221-232). Overall Assessment confirms: 'The two commits (4a92156b and 75906eee) successfully addressed the critical defects. The intent tables are well-designed with appropriate Section/Intent/What to Verify columns.'

expectations.text: Does NOT flag the preserved anti-pattern example (Hamza DM / compliance gap) as a defect
expectations.evidence: D1 section explicitly recognises the PakFreight/Hamza example as intentional: 'One intentional illustrative example retained (lines 246-269): The PakFreight LinkedIn DM is shown as a deliberate teaching example for the Compliance Gap concept... This correctly falls under the anti-pattern exception — the output exists to be critiqued, not to set expectations.' D1 count remains 0.

expectations.text: Does NOT flag the intent tables themselves as fabricated output
expectations.evidence: D1 is marked CLEAN with count 0. The intent tables are described as 'properly implemented' and 'well-designed with appropriate Section/Intent/What to Verify columns.' They are treated as correct replacements, not as fabricated output.

expectations.text: Identifies the lesson as mostly clean / low defect count
expectations.evidence: Summary table shows 'Total defects found: 4 (0 critical, 4 minor)'. Overall Assessment states: 'This lesson is in good shape post-fix.' Recommendation is only '~2 minutes of edits across 3 locations.'

expectations.text: If any defects remain, correctly categorises them using the 6-type taxonomy
expectations.evidence: All 6 defect types (D1-D6) are evaluated in the summary table. 4 minor defects found: 2x D2 (Missing Skill Name in Prompt — lines 239-242 and 300-309, prompts lack explicit skill name in the code block) and 2x D6 (Plugin/Tool Terminology — line 348, 'Claude' instead of 'Cowork' and missing 'Marketing' in plugin list). Categorisations are correct: the prompt blocks missing skill names match D2 definition, and the Cowork/Claude terminology mismatch matches D6.

claims.claim: Two intent tables are properly implemented at lines 205-215 and 221-232
claims.evidence: Report provides specific line ranges and describes the table structure (Section/Intent/What to Verify columns) and disclaimers (:::note Your output will vary). Cannot verify line numbers without reading the source lesson, but the structural description is internally consistent.

claims.claim: PakFreight illustrative example is properly disclaimed with :::note Illustrative example at lines 271-273
claims.evidence: Report provides specific line reference and quotes the disclaimer type. The narrative analysis (lines 275-281) is described as critiquing the example, which matches anti-pattern exception design.

claims.claim: Two D2 defects exist: prompts at lines 239-242 and 300-309 lack skill names
claims.evidence: Report quotes both prompt blocks verbatim and shows they lack a skill name reference. The surrounding narrative mentions the skill but the code blocks themselves do not contain it. The recommended fixes are provided.

claims.claim: Line 348 says 'Claude' instead of 'Cowork' and omits 'Marketing' from the plugin name
claims.evidence: Report quotes line 348: 'Use these prompts in Claude or your preferred AI assistant with the Sales and RevOps extension plugins installed.' Both issues (Claude→Cowork, missing Marketing) are correctly identified per cowork-content.md rules.

claims.claim: Total effort to fix is ~2 minutes of edits across 3 locations
claims.evidence: 3 locations: two D2 prompt blocks (add 'Use the outreach skill to' prefix) and one D6 line (change 'Claude' to 'Cowork' and add 'Marketing'). These are indeed trivial text insertions.

suggestions.assertion: Does NOT flag the preserved anti-pattern example (Hamza DM / compliance gap) as a defect
suggestions.reason: This is the strongest assertion in the set — it tests whether the skill understands the nuanced distinction between a fabricated output (D1 defect) and an intentional illustrative example that exists to be critiqued. It passed convincingly here. However, consider adding a negative variant: an eval where the anti-pattern example is NOT properly disclaimed, to verify the skill would flag it in that case.

No assertion checks whether the skill correctly identified the D2 and D6 minor defects. The current assertions only check that the skill didn't over-flag (false positives) and recognised the lesson as clean. Adding an expectation like 'Identifies at least one genuine minor defect' would verify the skill isn't just rubber-stamping everything as clean.

eval_feedback.overall: The eval effectively tests the hardest part of this scenario — distinguishing between fabricated outputs, intent tables, and intentional anti-pattern examples. The gap is on the true-positive side: no assertion verifies the skill can still find real (minor) defects in an already-fixed lesson.
